deliverables.text: A labeled Venn diagram of the Pell-eligible and state-grant-eligible sets, all four regions.
A worked union-and-intersection calculation using the union-intersection formula, cross-checked against D1.
A subset-and-empty-set argument: intersection as a subset of both eligibility sets, plus identification of the empty set under Order A and the non-empty set under Order B.
A renewal-count projection table for both orders, broken out by region, using the mailed/unmailed renewal rates.
A total-cost table for both orders: pieces mailed, cost per piece, total spent, dollars per on-time renewal.
A one-paragraph comparison of total on-time renewals under each order and the percentage margin between them.

balance.argument_a: Order A reaches every eligible student (the full union, 3,250 students) and produces 2,275 projected on-time renewals under Modeling Assumptions MA4/MA5, versus 1,988 under Order B -- a real gap of 287 students who keep aid they would otherwise lose, for $1,517.75 of university money.
balance.argument_b: Order B costs the university exactly $0.00 and still reaches the highest-need overlap group (1,336 students eligible for both programs), producing 1,988 of the 2,275 renewals Order A would produce -- roughly 87% of Order A's outcome at 0% of Order A's university cost, leaving the rest of the year's $1,600 discretionary budget untouched.
balance.margin_basis: The literal primary_metric (university dollars spent per on-time renewal) is degenerate for Order B, since its university-side cost is $0.00 by design -- any ratio against that numerator is $0.00 regardless of outcome, so it cannot be the two-sided comparison SPEC S2 requires. The formal balance/margin figure is computed instead on total on-time renewals achieved, which is well-defined and comparable for both orders: (2275-1988)/2275 = 12.6%. The $/renewal figures (Order A $0.67, Order B $0.00) remain in the case as Deliverable D5 -- a real, honest data point students must reckon with, not a hidden one.
balance.sensitivity_caveat: Tier 2 probe 5 (+/-50% flex on every declared Modeling Assumption) found the winner is NOT stable: a +50% flex on MA4 (no-reminder rate) or a -50% flex on MA5 (with-reminder rate) both flip the recommendation to Order B, and several other flexes push the margin past SPEC 2's 20% cap. This is disclosed, not hidden -- see sensitivity_disclosure[] (all Category F, irreducible unknowns) -- and it is consistent with the Modeling Assumptions table itself, which already marks MA2-MA5 'the answer is sensitive to this value.' A Hero who treats the 12.6% margin as rock-solid has missed this; FACILITATOR.md's Anchor 4 exists to surface it before the numbers are worked.

modeling_assumptions.statement: Cascade State's aid-renewal population is 9,000 continuing undergraduates.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Not sensitive -- scales mailed and renewal counts proportionally; the graded metrics are rates and margins, not the raw population.

modeling_assumptions.basis: Statewide CA ratio: 453,000 Cal Grant recipients [S4] / 2,440,631 CA undergraduates [S5].

modeling_assumptions.statement: 80% of state-eligible students are also Pell-eligible.
modeling_assumptions.basis: Qualitative: Cal Grant B's income ceiling is well inside the range where most families still clear at least a partial Pell award.

modeling_assumptions.statement: On-time renewal rate with no mailed reminder.
modeling_assumptions.basis: No public full-cycle baseline exists; set as the lower rate in the pair, informed by real reminder-effect research in Appendix D.

modeling_assumptions.statement: On-time renewal rate with a mailed reminder.
modeling_assumptions.basis: 15-point lift over MA4, informed by the direction/scale of a real RCT (Appendix D, [S8]), not a literal transfer of that study's own percentages.

modeling_assumptions.statement: Cascade State's total discretionary outreach mailing budget for the year.
modeling_assumptions.basis: Stated scenario constraint sized so Order A is affordable but consumes nearly all of it.

sensitivity_note: Routine administrative/financial-aid math. SPEC §6 was checked directly and does not apply -- this is neither an illness/death/family-hardship subject nor a protected-category framing; it is standard higher-ed operations math. No facilitator content warning required.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: MA2's 18.6% state-eligible share is anchored to California's real statewide Cal Grant ratio, but no public per-campus figure exists for a specific university's own income profile -- Cascade State's true share cannot be known in advance by any amount of research, only estimated from the statewide rate. A -50% flex pushes the total-renewals margin to 20.2%, just past the SPEC 2 20% cap, without flipping the winner.

MA3's 80% Pell/state overlap is a qualitative estimate -- no public dataset measures the real Pell/Cal-Grant overlap for any named university, and the true figure cannot be known in advance, only reasoned about from the two programs' income ceilings. A -50% flex pushes the margin to 21.6%, just past the SPEC 2 20% cap, without flipping the winner.

MA4's 55% no-reminder baseline renewal rate has no public full-cycle study to anchor it exactly -- the true rate for Cascade State's own population is an irreducible unknown, set only within the range implied by the real reminder-effect RCT in Appendix D. A +50% flex (to 82.5%) flips the winner to Order B, and a -50% flex pushes the margin to 55.5%. This is the case's most load-bearing assumption.

MA5's 70% with-reminder renewal rate is set as a 15-point lift over MA4, informed by the direction and scale (not the literal percentages) of a real RCT that measured a different channel (email, not mail) and a different window (20-day submission, not full-cycle renewal) -- the true value for a mailed reminder's effect on Cascade State's own renewal cycle cannot be known in advance. A -50% flex (to 35%) flips the winner to Order B, and either direction of flex pushes the margin past the SPEC 2 20% cap.

cohort_bands.note: Run the full anchor ladder as written: Anchor 1 cold-call vote, Anchors 2-4 as whole-room discussion, then split into two desks for D4/D5 before reconvening. The Deep Conflict two-thread block (20:00-30:00) works best split across two halves of the room, one thread each, then swap findings.

Skip the desk split for D4/D5 -- work them as one shared table on the board instead of two parallel desks; there usually is not the headcount to make two independent desks meaningful. Run both Deep Conflict threads sequentially with the whole group rather than splitting.

Anchor 1 becomes a stated initial position, not a cold-call vote. The facilitator argues the opposite order directly rather than cold-calling other Heroes. Both Deep Conflict threads still run, but as direct back-and-forth rather than room debate.
